item.research_question: How can a data-driven protocol be established to measure the similarity between materials based on specific physical properties to uncover underlying mechanisms and improve property prediction?
item.material_system: Three datasets: (1) 239 binary AB materials with Fm-3m (NaCl) structure; (2) 1541 binary AB body-centred cubic (b.c.c.) crystals; (3) 101 binary rare earth–transition metal alloys.
item.processing_route: Three-step protocol: (i) Kernel ridge regression (GKR) with exhaustive search of all variable combinations (e.g., 2^17-1 = 131,071 combinations) and 3x10-fold cross-validation to select combinations with R^2 > 0.90; (ii) Regression-based clustering using sparse linear regression (L1 regularization) and K-means modifications to partition data into k clusters; (iii) Construction of a committee machine from clustering results to generate an affinity matrix for hierarchical clustering.
item.test_conditions: Experiment 1: Formation energy (E_form) prediction; Experiment 2: Lattice constant (L_const) prediction; Experiment 3: Curie temperature (T_C) prediction. Calculations performed on a high-performance cluster (256 cores, 1.1 TB RAM).
key_findings: In Experiment 1, the R^2 score for formation energy prediction improved from 0.972 (MAE: 0.117 eV) to 0.982 (MAE: 0.101 eV) by using similarity-based regression.
In Experiment 2, the R^2 score for lattice constant prediction improved marginally from 0.991 (MAE: 0.013 Å) to 0.992 (MAE: 0.011 Å).
In Experiment 3, the R^2 score for Curie temperature prediction improved significantly from 0.974 (MAE: 37.87 K) to 0.991 (MAE: 24.16 K).
The method identified distinct material groups: G1 (oxides, nitrides, carbides with specific oxidation states) and G2 (halides, oxides, etc.) in the Fm-3m dataset.
For b.c.c. crystals, three groups were identified: G1 (heavy transition metals), G2 (metal and non-metal), and G3 (metal and non-metal with different lattice constant dependencies).
For rare earth–transition metal alloys, G1 included high T_C Mn- and Co-based alloys, while G2 included Fe-based Fe17RE2 alloys.
The affinity matrix values ranged from 0 (never in same cluster) to 1 (always in same cluster), with intra-group affinities exceeding 0.7 and inter-group affinities below 0.2 in Experiment 1.
item.mechanism: The authors argue that materials belonging to the same cluster in the regression-based models share the same 'actuating mechanisms' for the target physical property. By constructing a committee machine that votes on cluster membership across multiple high-accuracy regression models, the method captures multilateral similarities that reflect the underlying physics, allowing for more accurate local linear modeling when predicting properties for new materials.
item.limitations: The exhaustive search for variable selection based on kernel regression consumes significant computing resources (e.g., 36, 41, and 28 hours for the three experiments) due to combinatorial explosion. Additionally, no significant improvement in R^2 was observed for the lattice constant prediction problem compared to the other two properties.
item.future_work: The text states the method can 'systematically facilitate further understanding of a given phenomenon by identifying similarities among materials' and implies future application to other properties, but does not explicitly list specific future work projects beyond the general utility of the protocol.
quotes: The method consists of three steps: variable evaluation based on nonlinear regression, regression-based clustering, and similarity measurement with a committee machine constructed from the clustering results.
The experiments show that rational and meaningful group structures can be obtained and that the prediction accuracy of the materials' physical properties can be significantly increased.

The obtained results provide significant evidence to support our hypothesis that the similarity measured by the committee machine reflects the similarity in the actuating mechanisms of the target material physical property.
